name: hex-simd
verdict_reason: The dashboard shows hex-simd 18x faster at encoding (4 KiB) and 23x faster at decoding (1 KiB) than the hex crate, and about 6x faster at 16 bytes. hex 0.4.3 has not had a release since 2021, so the gap to the default still stands; const-hex's separate benchmark also shows hex an order of magnitude behind SIMD hex crates.
tier_reason: First-party dashboard generated by CI; benchmark code is public but the CPU and toolchain are not stated.
claimed_speedup: encode 14.389 vs 0.793 GiB/s at 4096 bytes (18x), 3.711 vs 0.607 GiB/s at 16 bytes (6.1x); decode 15.283 vs 0.660 GiB/s at 1024 bytes (23x), 3.425 vs 0.602 GiB/s at 16 bytes (5.7x) (ratios derived from page data)
workload: Hex encode and decode of 16-byte to 4 KiB buffers with runtime-detected SIMD vs hex's scalar code.
platforms: runtime-dispatched SIMD on x86/x86_64, aarch64 and wasm; scalar fallback
one_liner: SIMD hex encoder/decoder measured 18x-23x faster than the hex crate on 1-4 KiB inputs by its author.
how_it_is_fast: Processes whole SIMD registers of input per step, with kernels chosen at runtime; decoding and validation follow the vectorized hex-parsing approach in Wojciech Muła's article cited in the README.
use_it_when: Encoding or decoding hex in bulk (hashes, binary dumps) where hex 0.4 is a hotspot
You also want SIMD check-only validation
skip_it_when: You want a crate with recent releases: last hex-simd release is 0.8.0 (2022-12-28)
You prefer a drop-in API for hex: const-hex mirrors hex's API
caveats: First-party numbers from 2023-04 with no hardware stated
hex/fallback decode at 4096 bytes (0.293 GiB/s) is lower than at 1024 bytes, which suggests noise in that cell
faster-hex in this dashboard is pre-1.0; faster-hex 1.0 (2026-09) was rewritten
tradeoffs: The README says the project relies heavily on unsafe code

evidence.quote: This project relies heavily on unsafe code.
